description:

implemented:
- 429 rate from Z.AI > 5% over 5m -> alert (quota pressure)
- p95 latency > 10s -> alert (upstream degradation)
- Error rate > 2% -> alert

Alertmanager is already running in-cluster on ardenone-cluster (confirmed live,
monitoring namespace) and Prometheus already scrapes zai-proxy via the existing
ServiceMonitor (k8s/ardenone-cluster/devpod/zai-proxy-servicemonitor.yml), so this is
pure config, no new infra.

Add a PrometheusRule (e.g.
k8s/ardenone-cluster/devpod/zai-proxy-alerts-prometheusrule.yml in
jedarden/declarative-config) with the three rules above using the existing metrics
(zai_proxy_upstream_errors_total{error_type="429"}, request duration histogram,
zai_proxy_requests_total by status_code), labeled so they route through the existing
Alertmanager config.

Motivation: this exact gap - "something silently broke and nobody found out until an
unrelated audit" - is precisely what happened to zai-proxy-dashboard itself (see bf-2fgl,
down 51-64 days with no alert firing). Closing this gap for the proxy's own quota/error
signals prevents the same class of silent failure on the proxy side.

title: Restore zai-proxy-dashboard: 51-64 day production outage (devpod/ardenone-cluster)
description:
Live-artifact check on 2026-07-20 found zai-proxy-dashboard non-functional in production:

- Pod zai-proxy-dashboard-5ff6b485f-* : CrashLoopBackOff, 14500+ restarts over 51 days.
  Logs: "failed to initialize storage: failed to enable WAL mode: unable to open database
  file: out of memory (14)"
- Pod zai-proxy-dashboard-b9fd57878-* : stuck ContainerCreating for 36 days — a second
  ReplicaSet from a failed rollout, contending for the same ReadWriteOnce PVC
  (zai-proxy-dashboard-data, Longhorn storageClass) as the crashlooping pod.
- Public URL https://zai-dash.ardenone.com/ returns 503 "no available server" (confirmed
  via direct curl).

This is a GitOps-managed deployment (jedarden/declarative-config,
k8s/ardenone-cluster/devpod/zai-proxy-dashboard.yml) on ardenone-cluster, synced by
ArgoCD. No live kubectl mutation was performed — fix must land via a
declarative-config commit + ArgoCD sync, per this workspace's rules.

Likely near-term fix options (pick one, evaluate in declarative-config):
1. Delete/recreate the zai-proxy-dashboard-data PVC (check first whether the underlying
   Longhorn volume is in the fleet's known-faulted set) and force a clean single-ReplicaSet
   rollout (e.g. bump a pod-template annotation to force replacement of both stuck
   ReplicaSets).
2. Temporarily switch the volume from the PVC to emptyDir to unblock service while the
   permanent architecture fix (ADR-1, docs/plan/plan.md) is implemented.

This is a tactical restore — the durable fix is the storage architecture change tracked
in ADR-1 (docs/plan/plan.md, "ADR-1: Dashboard metrics storage") and its own follow-up
bead for the stateless rewrite.

Verification: after the fix, curl -s https://zai-dash.ardenone.com/healthz should return
200, and kubectl get pods -n devpod should show a single Running zai-proxy-dashboard pod.

  by dashboard/api (so /api/metrics, /api/status, and the SSE hub need no changes).
- dashboard/main.go: remove the fatal os.Exit(1) storage-init path since there is no
  longer an external dependency that can fail this way.

  zai-proxy-dashboard-data PVC, the storageClassName: longhorn PVC spec, and the
  volumeMount — commit there once code ships and image is built, let ArgoCD sync.

  describe the new in-memory design instead of SQLite/WAL.

Depends on / motivated by bf-2fgl (tactical outage restore) — this is the durable fix
referenced from ADR-1.

window is fine), and existing dashboard Go tests pass against the new storage backend.

title: Proxy handler logic duplicated: production uses main.go inline handler, tests only exercise handler.go ProxyHandler

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
Gap found during plan-vs-artifacts audit.

EVIDENCE
- Production request-serving pipeline (concurrency cap -> AIMD rate limit -> body capture -> token counting -> TranslateRequest -> retry loop -> response validation -> X-Token-Input header) is implemented inline as http.HandleFunc("/", ...) in proxy/main.go (roughly lines 326-750, wired by main() at line 205).
- A second, struct-based copy of the same pipeline exists as ProxyHandler.ServeHTTP in proxy/handler.go (NewProxyHandler + ~507 lines).
- NewProxyHandler is constructed ONLY from tests: proxy/helpers_test.go and proxy/retry_test.go. No non-test file references ProxyHandler/NewProxyHandler.
- Result: the retry / rate-limit / concurrency integration tests validate handler.go, but production serves the main.go inline handler. The two implementations can drift silently (e.g. a retry/backoff or capacity fix applied to one and not the other), and the code path that actually carries traffic is not the one under test.
- Also note the stale inline comment in main.go ('strip Anthropic API fields ZhipuAI doesn't support') contradicts the plan, which states TranslateRequest is a documented no-op; consolidating removes the divergent copy.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Single source of truth for the proxy request pipeline: main() constructs and serves the same handler type the tests exercise (or the inline handler and ProxyHandler are merged into one), so production and tests run identical code.
- No production-only or test-only copy of the retry/rate-limit/concurrency/token-counting logic remains.
- Existing proxy tests still pass against the consolidated handler; add a test that drives the production-wired handler end to end if not already present.
- Plan/code comments about TranslateRequest reconciled to the no-op reality.

title: zai-proxy-v2 (production) runs as a single replica with no redundancy - add HPA or minReplicas=2
description:
The production proxy Deployment (zai-proxy-v2, the sole path from cluster workloads to
the Z.AI API) runs replicas: 1 with no HPA, in
k8s/ardenone-cluster/devpod/zai-proxy-v2.yml. A HorizontalPodAutoscaler manifest exists
(zai-proxy-hpa.yml.disabled) but targets the retired zai-proxy Deployment (which is
permanently scaled to 0 - "service routes to v2 only"), so it is effectively dead
config pointed at the wrong object.

Since every LLM-calling agent in the cluster depends on this single pod, a single node
drain, OOM, or crash currently takes down all Z.AI access cluster-wide with zero
redundancy. Resource requests are tiny (32Mi/10m per pod per zai-proxy-v2.yml), so
running 2+ replicas is cheap.

Fix (in jedarden/declarative-config):
1. Point a corrected HPA (or just replicas: 2 for simplicity, given how small the
   ceiling is) at zai-proxy-v2, and delete/retire the stale
   zai-proxy-hpa.yml.disabled once superseded.
2. Confirm the AdaptiveRateLimiter's global ceiling state doesn't assume a single
   process (check proxy/main.go - if the rate limiter is in-process state, 2 replicas
   means the *effective* combined rate could exceed RATE_LIMIT_MAX; may need to divide
   the configured ceiling across replica count, or accept the headroom given
   RATE_LIMIT_MAX=7 is already conservative versus Z.AI's real limit).

Related to bf-c8yh (rate limiter fairness) - both touch proxy/main.go's rate limiter
assumptions.

title: Add unit tests for retry / response-validation paths with a mock upstream
description:
docs/plan/plan.md documents a precise error-classification contract (sections: 'Retry logic', 'Response validation', 'Error classification' table), but there are no unit tests for it — grep for retry/429 in proxy/main_test.go and proxy/bodyparser_test.go finds nothing. The only coverage is live-cluster shell scripts under proxy/tests/, which NEEDLE/CI cannot run.

Scope — Go unit tests in proxy/ using net/http/httptest as a fake upstream, driving the real proxy handler:
- 429 with Retry-After header: the header delay is honoured before the next attempt, then success is returned to the client
- 429 without Retry-After: exponential backoff retry up to MAX_RETRIES, then the 429 is surfaced
- 2xx with empty or invalid JSON body (non-streaming): retried, 502 after MAX_RETRIES
- Streaming response opening with zero bytes: retried, 502 after MAX_RETRIES
- 422: NOT retried, passed through to the client (exactly one upstream call observed)
- Other 4xx/5xx: passed through with no retry
- Retry attempts increment zai_proxy_retry_attempts_total with the correct reason label, and errors increment zai_proxy_upstream_errors_total with the correct error_type

Constraints:
- Z.AI-specific behavior stays as-is — do not generalize; no quota/rate-limit headers exist upstream beyond 429/Retry-After
- Shrink backoff delays for tests via injection or tiny MAX_RETRIES/env rather than sleeping seconds; suite must stay fast
- Never hit the real api.z.ai in tests

Acceptance criteria:
- New test file(s) in proxy/ covering every row of the plan's error-classification table
- Upstream call counts asserted per case (e.g. 422 => 1 call, empty-body => 1+MAX_RETRIES calls)
- go test ./... passes with -race

title: Add unit tests for AdaptiveRateLimiter (AIMD/EWMA) in proxy
description:
The adaptive rate limiter is the core reliability mechanism described in docs/plan/plan.md (section: 'Global adaptive rate limiter (AIMD/EWMA)'), but it has zero unit tests. proxy/main_test.go + metrics_test.go contain 64 test functions and none exercise AdaptiveRateLimiter (proxy/main.go: type AdaptiveRateLimiter, NewAdaptiveRateLimiter, Wait, Record429, RecordSuccess, tryAdjustRate, GetCurrentRate, Reset).

Scope — table-driven Go unit tests in proxy/ covering:
- Rate stays within [minRate, maxRate] bounds under any 429/success sequence
- 429-rate > 5% in a window: EWMA ceiling update (alpha default 0.3) and drop to ceiling * (1 - hold_margin)
- 429-rate < 1%: convergence toward hold position in 50% steps per window
- Probe above ceiling after probe_interval clean windows
- Reset() restores the initial rate
- Wait() returns sane durations and Record429/RecordSuccess are safe under concurrent use (run with -race)
- Env tunables RATE_LIMIT_CEILING_ALPHA / RATE_LIMIT_HOLD_MARGIN / RATE_LIMIT_PROBE_INTERVAL are parsed and applied

Constraints (IMPORTANT):
- The limiter is deliberately Z.AI-specific — do NOT refactor it into a generic multi-provider abstraction
- Z.AI exposes no quota endpoint or rate-limit response headers; the only upstream signal is HTTP 429 (+ optional Retry-After). Tests must not invent quota/limit headers
- Prefer injecting time/window boundaries or calling tryAdjustRate directly over sleeping in tests; keep the suite fast (<5s)
- Minimal, test-only refactors of proxy/main.go are acceptable (e.g. making window duration configurable for tests); no behavior changes

Acceptance criteria:
- New proxy/ratelimiter_test.go (or additions to main_test.go) with the cases above
- go test ./... passes with -race
- No changes to the limiter's production behavior or defaults

title: Add per-source fairness to the global adaptive rate limiter
description:
proxy/main.go's AdaptiveRateLimiter is a single global token bucket shared by every
caller (documented in docs/plan/plan.md: "A single token-bucket limiter serves all
traffic"). There is no per-agent authentication by design, but that also means one
noisy caller (a runaway NEEDLE worker, a retry storm) can consume the entire
RATE_LIMIT_MAX budget (7 req/s in production - see zai-proxy-v2 env) and starve every
other caller sharing the proxy.

Add lightweight fairness on top of the existing limiter, without adding per-agent auth:
- Key in-flight/waiting requests by a coarse identity signal already available without
  new auth (e.g. source pod IP from cluster-internal DNS, or a caller-supplied
  X-Client-Id header that is not treated as a credential).
- Round-robin or weighted-fair-queue across keys when the global rate is saturated,
  instead of first-come-first-served.
- Expose a per-key wait-time or rejection metric (extend
  zai_proxy_rate_limit_rejections_total with a client label, cardinality-bounded).

Keep the existing global ceiling/EWMA logic (proxy/main.go AdaptiveRateLimiter) as the
outer bound - this is about fairness *within* that budget, not raising it.

title: Consolidate confusing zai-proxy / zai-proxy-v2 / zai-proxy-canary naming into a single clear production Deployment
description:

confusing enough that docs/plan/plan.md has to call it out explicitly: the "zai-proxy"
Deployment is permanently scaled to 0 (replicas: 0, "original Deployment"), while
"zai-proxy-v2" is the actual production workload, and "zai-proxy-canary" is the real
canary. Anyone doing on-call triage who scales up "zai-proxy" expecting it to be
production, or who greps for "the prod deployment" and finds the empty one first, will
be misled - this is exactly the kind of drift that let the dashboard outage (bf-2fgl)
go unnoticed.

Proposed cleanup (in jedarden/declarative-config, coordinate with an actual
maintenance window since this touches the live routing Service):
- Rename "zai-proxy-v2" Deployment to "zai-proxy" (the name matching the Service that
  actually selects it via app: zai-proxy), and retire/delete the empty "zai-proxy"
  (v1, replicas=0) Deployment and its now-superseded zai-proxy-hpa.yml.disabled
  entirely rather than leaving them as scaled-to-zero fossils.
- Update docs/plan/plan.md's Deployment section and Repository Layout table to match.

Lower priority than the correctness/outage beads (bf-2fgl, bf-4gev) - this is pure
operational clarity/hygiene, not a live bug.
